data_flow: User interactions in NavigationSplitView → CustomModeEngine profile mutations → NSWorkspace app picker queries → engine state updates reflected in sidebar selection and detail editor
name: PowerMate Custom Mode Configuration UI
summary: Renders the SwiftUI configuration interface for PowerMate's custom mode with profile management and per-application binding. Drives the CustomModeEngine for profile CRUD and queries NSWorkspace for app selection. Fixed window dimensions and fragile profile identification create layout and correctness risks.
tech_debt_summary: New profile detection relies on engine.profiles.last append assumption; fixed 750×520 frame clips on small displays; activationPolicy filter excludes menu bar and background apps users may want to control.

data_flow: VolumeController/BrightnessController emit level changes → OSDOverlay creates/updates HUD window with fade animation → display token cancels prior overlay → automatic timer dismisses after delay
name: macOS OSD HUD Overlay
summary: Renders native-style macOS on-screen display panels for volume and brightness feedback. Receives level updates from audio and brightness controllers, animates translucent HUD windows with SF Symbols icons and segmented level bars on the active screen.
tech_debt_summary: High-risk force unwrap on NSScreen fallback; missing accessibility/VoiceOver support; timer scheduling lacks RunLoop mode specification; unverified custom view implementations.

data_flow: Process launch → signal handlers registered → NSApplication configured as accessory → delegate assigned to AppDelegate.shared → run loop starts → signals trigger exit() with no gamma cleanup guarantee
name: macOS Cocoa Bootstrap & Signal Handler
summary: Bootstraps a headless macOS accessory application with no dock icon, installs POSIX signal handlers for graceful gamma restoration on SIGINT/SIGTERM, and delegates lifecycle control to AppDelegate. Uses manual NSApplication delegate assignment rather than the standard NSApplicationMain attribute.
tech_debt_summary: Critical: async-signal-unsafe exit() in handler risks corruption; deprecated signal() API without SA_RESTART; no SIGKILL or crash recovery path leaves display gamma altered; unguarded force-unwrap of AppDelegate.shared in signal handler.

data_flow: CustomModeEngine triggers send → OSCController resolves or reuses cached NWConnection → serializes typed arguments with 4-byte OSC string padding → transmits UDP packet
name: OSC Network Message Sender
summary: Transmits UDP-based OSC messages to external audio and control hardware using Network.framework. Caches persistent connections per host:port endpoint to reduce connection overhead on repeated sends. Triggered by the action engine during custom mode execution.
tech_debt_summary: Force-unwrapped port initialization risks crashes; no connection cleanup on failure or idle timeout; missing OSC bundle support for synchronized multi-message sends.

data_flow: Hardware input → knob/button state translation → CoreMIDI packet construction → virtual source endpoint → DAW; reverse path: action engine commands → CC value updates → LED level feedback
name: CoreMIDI Virtual Source Controller
summary: Exposes a hardware knob controller as a CoreMIDI virtual device, translating physical knob rotation into Control Change messages and button presses into Note On/Off events. Feeds normalized level data back to LED visualization and receives delta/absolute adjustments from the action engine.
tech_debt_summary: Thread-unsafe shared state for CC values and note flags; implicit self capture in MIDI callback; hardcoded 1024-byte packet buffer without size validation.

data_flow: Raw HID events from PowerMateUSBTransport/PowerMateBLETransport → temporal gesture analysis in PowerMateManager → semantic delegate callbacks → VolumeController applies volume/mute via CoreAudio → AppleScript/software fallback on failure → OSDOverlay for visual feedback
name: PowerMate Hardware & Audio Volume Controller
summary: Mediates gesture input from USB/BLE PowerMate dials into semantic press, double-tap, and rotation events while driving LED state across all transports. Falls back through six volume control strategies—CoreAudio, AppleScript, software gain—to maintain audio control when hardware mute is unavailable. Timer-based gesture detection and AppleScript debouncing carry reliability risks under system pressure.
tech_debt_summary: Timer-based gesture detection vulnerable to coalescing and background throttling; AppleScript rate limiter loses intermediate volume values during rapid changes and permanently disables fallback due to unreset failure counter; simulated mute state not persisted across restarts.

data_flow: Release metadata (version, build, signature, notes URL) is manually entered into appcast.xml → Sparkle framework polls feed on client devices → clients verify EdDSA signature and download DMG via referenced URLs
name: Sparkle Appcast Feed
summary: Publishes versioned software update metadata as a live RSS appcast for PowerMateReborn, embedding EdDSA signatures and build numbers for Sparkle framework consumption. References external release notes and release artifacts hosted on GitHub Pages. Template comments indicate manual editing workflow for future releases.
tech_debt_summary: Template workflow is partially ignored (newest release placed after template comment, not before); missing sparkle:minimumSystemVersion on published releases despite template inclusion; hardcoded GitHub raw URL risks breakage on repository transfer or rename.

data_flow: Template is consumed by build-dmg.sh during release generation → placeholders are replaced with actual release artifacts → produces live appcast.xml for Sparkle framework consumption
name: Sparkle Appcast Template
summary: Defines the canonical XML template for Sparkle RSS appcast entries used in macOS auto-update distribution. Standardizes release metadata structure including version, signature, and minimum OS requirements for the release-pipeline to populate during builds.
tech_debt_summary: Channel link diverges from live appcast URL structure; missing placeholders for minimumSystemVersion update guidance and releaseNotesLink that live appcast uses.

data_flow: Developer runs shell commands to generate EdDSA keys → signs DMG with private key → manually edits appcast XML with release metadata → pushes XML to GitHub Pages for Sparkle client polling
name: Sparkle Auto-Update Release Pipeline
summary: Configures EdDSA signing and GitHub Pages appcast hosting for macOS delta updates. Publishes signed DMG releases with manual XML feed edits. Hardcoded repository paths and version strings create brittle release steps.
tech_debt_summary: Manual XML editing without validation for security-critical fields; hardcoded GitHub username, repository path, and version strings throughout; no documented key backup or rotation procedure.

data_flow: Static configuration consumed at build time by SPM → resolves Sparkle dependency and system framework linkages → emits compiled executable with bundled resources for runtime hardware access
name: PowerMate Driver Package Manifest
summary: Defines the Swift Package Manager build configuration for a macOS hardware-interfacing executable that integrates Sparkle auto-updates and links system frameworks for audio, Bluetooth, and HID device access. Consumed by the application bootstrap and lifecycle subsystems during compilation, and referenced by release pipeline scripts for DMG generation and Sparkle setup documentation.
tech_debt_summary: Sparkle dependency lacks platform condition despite macOS-only linking; potential over-linking of CoreAudio-related frameworks that may not all be exercised by code paths.

data_flow: CoreBluetooth scan results → CBPeripheral connection → service/characteristic discovery → notification parsing for rotation/button events → PowerMateManager; LED commands flow downward via write to proprietary characteristic
name: PowerMate BLE Transport
summary: Scans, connects, and parses BLE events from the Griffin PowerMate Bluetooth device. Exposes rotation and button events to the input gesture engine and accepts LED brightness commands. Implementation is truncated mid-file with incomplete delegate methods.
tech_debt_summary: CBPeripheralDelegate implementation is incomplete (file truncated). Missing connection timeout, retry limits, and force-unwrap on NWEndpoint.Port initialization.

data_flow: Package.swift version → Swift compilation → .app bundle assembly with Sparkle framework → Info.plist generation with EdDSA key → code signing (inside-out) → extended attribute stripping → DMG creation → output to update-distribution
name: macOS DMG Builder & Code Signer
summary: Compiles Swift binaries into signed .app bundles and packages them into distributable DMG images for Sparkle auto-update. Integrates with the build-and-distribution subsystem for version metadata and feeds the update-distribution subsystem with signed artifacts.
tech_debt_summary: Hardcoded Sparkle framework path and literal developer identity require per-builder script edits; missing codesign verification before DMG creation; stale 1.1.0 version fallback; rpath duplication risk on repeated builds.

data_flow: Build artifact enters → codesign with hardened runtime → DMG creation → Apple notarization upload → staple notarization ticket → publish to GitHub Releases → generate Sparkle appcast with EdDSA signature
name: macOS Code Signing & Release Orchestrator
summary: Documents the complete workflow for signing, notarizing, and distributing the PowerMateReborn macOS application. Covers Apple Developer ID certificate provisioning, hardened runtime codesigning, DMG packaging, Apple notarization with stapling, and Sparkle auto-update integration via EdDSA signatures. The guide serves as the single source of truth for release engineers but contains version inconsistencies between documented examples.
tech_debt_summary: Hardcoded version string mismatch between DMG filename and GitHub release tag in documentation examples; certificate name contains literal personal identifier requiring manual replacement per user; quick reference section duplicates substantial content violating DRY principle.

data_flow: AppDelegate observes frontmost app → CustomModeEngine loads matching profile → rotary/button events trigger action dispatch → MIDIController or OSCController emits hardware/network messages
name: PowerMate Custom Mode Action Engine
summary: Dispatches profile-driven knob and button actions for the PowerMate hardware, switching configurations per frontmost application. Persists Codable mapping configs to disk and routes scroll, keyboard, media, MIDI, and OSC events to downstream controllers.
tech_debt_summary: Flat CodableActionConfig struct causes serialization bloat; CC accumulator keys lack channel disambiguation risking collision; no validation of bundle identifiers against installed apps.

data_flow: Display probe enumerates up to 16 displays → VCP write requests enter pendingWrites queue → coalesceTimers batch and deduplicate → dlopen'd IOAVService I2C functions transmit to monitor hardware
name: Apple Silicon DDC Monitor Controller
summary: Controls external monitor brightness, volume, and contrast via DDC/CI over I2C on Apple Silicon Macs. Dynamically loads private IOKit IOAVService APIs to send VCP codes, with aggressive rate limiting and write coalescing to prevent bus saturation. Consumed by BrightnessController for display-brightness-control subsystem integration.
tech_debt_summary: High-risk reliance on private IOAVService APIs via dynamic loading; incomplete file truncation mid-implementation; no thread safety for pendingWrites/coalesceTimers dictionaries; fixed 16-display array risks buffer overflow.

data_flow: Display detection triggers capability probing → method selection (DisplayServices/DDC/gamma) → brightness commands dispatched per-display → gamma table backups stored in DisplayState for restoration
name: Multi-Strategy Display Brightness Controller
summary: Controls display brightness through automatic capability detection per display, falling back from private Apple APIs through DDC/CI hardware to software gamma overlays. Persists per-display preferences keyed by serial and supports synchronized multi-display operation. Unsafe private framework loading and memory leaks require hardening before production use.
tech_debt_summary: Critical: unsafe dlopen of private DisplayServices.framework without version checks, memory leak in reportBuffer, and no thread synchronization for shared display state. Probing mutates brightness causing visible flicker.

data_flow: AppDelegate requests icon by mode → MenuBarIcon composites geometric primitives with scaled SVG coordinates → returns CGImage for NSStatusItem
name: Menu Bar Vector Icon Renderer
summary: Renders Core Graphics vector icons for macOS menu bar status items. Generates four mode-specific Lucide-style symbols by compositing geometric primitives with SVG-coordinate scaling. Consumed by AppDelegate to populate the status bar.
tech_debt_summary: Degenerate line hack for dot rendering, no dark mode support, and magic numbers throughout without named constants.

data_flow: IOHIDManager device matching → 6-byte report parse (button bit-field, signed rotation delta) → PowerMateManager; LED commands ← PowerMateManager → 1-byte HID output report → device
name: PowerMate USB HID Transport
summary: Manages bidirectional IOKit HID communication with Griffin PowerMate USB devices, parsing 6-byte input reports for button and rotation events and driving LED state via output reports. Feeds decoded hardware events upstream to the input-gesture-engine and receives lifecycle signals from the application controller. Contains unverified memory management and blocking async patterns that risk leaks and stalls.
tech_debt_summary: Critical: unallocated UnsafeMutablePointer report buffer leaks memory, Unmanaged.passUnretained risks use-after-dealloc crashes, and force-unwrap of IOHIDManagerCreate result is unsafe. Secondary: startup LED test blocks global queue with usleep busy-wait, and input report length is unchecked.

data_flow: Documentation serves as entry point for developers navigating to HID drivers, volume/brightness engines, MIDI/OSC integration, and per-app profile subsystems

summary: Indexes the complete project structure for a native Swift menu bar app that restores Griffin PowerMate USB/Bluetooth controller functionality on modern macOS. Documents four operational modes (Volume, Brightness, MIDI, Custom) with gesture-based interaction and 10 key design decisions including userspace IOKit HID and adaptive audio fallback chains.

data_flow: User reads installation instructions → follows hardware compatibility checks → references research docs for deep-dive technical details → builds from source using documented instructions
name: PowerMateReborn Project Documentation
summary: Documents the native Swift menu bar application that restores Griffin PowerMate USB/Bluetooth controller functionality on modern macOS. Describes four control modes, hardware compatibility requirements, and build procedures for end users and contributors.
tech_debt_summary: High-severity contradiction between README and CODE_SIGNING.md on notarization status; beta Bluetooth support lacks validated hardware mapping; build instructions use mismatched directory name 'PowerMateDriver' instead of 'PowerMateReborn'.

data_flow: Hardware events from USB/BLE transports → PowerMateManager gesture parsing → mode-specific controller dispatch (Volume/Brightness/MIDI/Custom) → OSDOverlay feedback + MenuBarIcon status update → UserDefaults settings persistence on mode changes
name: Menu Bar Application Controller
summary: Orchestrates macOS menu-bar lifecycle for a PowerMate hardware utility, managing modal operation switching and transport initialization. Coordinates volume, brightness, MIDI, and custom mode engines through a dynamic status menu with connection-state SF Symbols. Persists user settings via UserDefaults and gates Sparkle auto-updater to standard .app bundle detection.
tech_debt_summary: Medium-risk force-unwrap on NSImage copy without nil check; low-risk hardcoded menu title fallback and brittle Sparkle bundle detection relying solely on pathExtension.
